messages.subject: Negative Binomial
parts:
Hi,

I need to run a geometric family model with inla.

x is the number of pacients, until we get one with influenza.


x <- c(4,0,6,3,2,0,1,6,5,6,1,4,19)

z is a covariable

z <- c(12,6,20,11,10,5,7,17,16,15,6,13,22)

form.a = x ~ 1+z

mod.a = inla(form.a,data=data.frame(x,z),family="nbinomial",
               control.fixed = list(mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.01,mean=0,prec=0.01),
               control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))


My question is: were or how do I state that I want a negative binomial with n = 1? I am counting the pacients until I get n=1 pacients with influenza.

Thank you so much,
Sílvia

Hello,

I've followed your advice, and implemented 

x <- c(4,0,6,3,2,0,1,6,5,6,1,4,19)
(x is the number of pacients, until we get one with influenza, z is a covariate)
mod.a = inla(form.a,data=data.frame(x,z),family="nbinomial2", Ntrials=1)

the results are as expected, but I need to specify prior distributions for the intercept, and the z-coefficient. Both should be Gaussian with zero mean and precision 0.01.

I've tried to do so by including the "blue" instruction in inla(.) :

mod.a = inla(form.a,data=data.frame(x,z),family="nbinomial",
               control.fixed = list(mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.01,mean=0,prec=0.01),
               control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))

Can I do that? 
Does this blue code makes INLA assuming zero mean and 0.01 precision for the normal priori distributions of the intercept and the covariate coefficient? 



After that, I need to run, for the same data x, a different model: a model with random effects.

The model is 
form.b = x ~ f(day,model="iid",param=c(1,0.01))

I have the instruction param=c(1,0.01) to model the precision tau of the random effect. 
The random effect is assumed to be Normal(mu,tau), 
and the precision tau is assumed to be Gamma(1,0.01). 

Based in your previous answer, I thought that maybe now I should run
mod.b = inla(form.b,data=data.frame(day=1:13,x),family="nbinomial2",Ntrials=1)

But I need a prior to mu as well, because mu is assumed to be a Normal(0,0.01).
I would like to know if I can do that by including the "blue" instruction:

mod.b1 = inla(form.b,data=data.frame(dia=1:13,x),family="nbinomial2",Ntrials=1,
             control.fixed = list(mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.01),
             control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))
Is it the right instruction?

I am reading the documents for inla, and the R-Project help, but I still have this questions...

Thank you for you kindness,
Sílvia Guerra

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Negative Binomial
parts:
On Tue, 2018-10-30 at 11:15 -0700, Silvia Isabel wrote:
> I've tried to do so by including the "blue" instruction in inla(.) :
>
> mod.a = inla(form.a,data=data.frame(x,z),family="nbinomial",
> control.fixed =
> list(mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=0.01,mean=0,prec=0.01),
> control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))
> Can I do that?
that is correct.

> Does this blue code makes INLA assuming zero mean and 0.01 precision
> for the normal priori distributions of the intercept and the
> covariate coefficient?

yes. If you have several of these with different values, then you can also use

f(z, model="linear", mean.linear = ..., prec.linear = ...)

see inla.doc("linear")

also, with a recent testing version you can do

inla.priors.used(mod.a)

to check that the priors used are the ones you want.

Best
H

--
